title: Atletico Madrid 2-0 Viking: Sorloth and Alvarez on target in much-needed win
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutAtletico Madrid 2-0 Viking: Sorloth and Alvarez on target in much-needed winShareAtletico Madrid secured a timely second win in the Champions League as they boosted their knockout hopes by brushing aside Viking.Atletico Madrid got their Champions League campaign back on track after first-half strikes from Alexander Sorloth and Julian Alvarez sealed a 2-0 win over 10-man Viking.
Having won just one of their four matches coming into Wednesday's clash, a clinical showing in the first 45 minutes bumped last year's semi-finalists up to 18th in the table.
Sorloth finally ended his goal drought before Alvarez's free-kick crept in at the near post, with Viking defender Henrik Falchener receiving a straight red card late in the day.
Both sides started brightly, but neither Jan Oblak nor Lubomir Belko were tested early on, though the Viking goalkeeper was picking the ball out of the net in the 19th minute.

Alejandro Grimaldo was slipped in behind the Viking defence before looking up and finding Sorloth, who brilliantly fired his left-footed effort beyond Belko for his first goal across all competitions this season.

Diego Simeone's side pulled further clear five minutes later. Alvarez's free-kick from the left-hand side looked to have been kept out by Belko before Alex Baena's follow-up was saved, but referee Erik Lambrechts glanced at his watch and gave the goal, with the ball having crossed the line.
Lee Kang-In and Baena then brought saves out of Belko at the end of the first half, with Grimaldo's dipping shot from distance awkwardly cleared away by the Viking goalkeeper.
The hosts thought they had a penalty on the hour when Johnny Cardoso was brought down by Peter Christiansen, but after a VAR review, the referee overturned his decision.

Belko continued to frustrate Atletico as he got down low to keep out Cardoso's volley, and while Simeone's side struggled to break down Viking's defence, the visitors' hopes of a comeback were dented when Falchener was sent off in stoppage time for a last-man foul on Giuliano Simeone.
Atletico win again at fortress Metropolitano
In a somewhat surprising start to their Champions League campaign, Atletico started MD5 outside the play-off places, but when Simeone's side play at home in Europe, they are a difficult side to beat.

Atletico have now won 11 of their last 14 home group-stage games in the Champions League (L3), scoring 2+ goals in 11 of these matches, while they have also won 10 of their last 15 matches against sides outside the top five European Leagues (D3 L2) in the competition, scoring 44 goals.

Simeone said ahead of kick-off Sorloth remained important to Atletico's vision despite failing to score in 2026-27, but he ended his wait for a goal here. The Norwegian has now been directly involved in seven goals (six goals, one assist) in his last six starts in the Champions League.

Alvarez also made his mark. Since joining Atletico in 2024-25, he has scored more direct free-kick goals (three) than any other player in the Champions League, and he is the second player to reach 25 goal involvements (19 goals, six assists) in the Champions League while playing for Atletico, after Antoine Griezmann (56).

Viking, meanwhile, have lost their first three away games in the Champions League, all by a two-goal margin, and they were second-best here. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 0.62 from nine shots to Atletico's tally of 1.88 from 20 attempts.
